## Detailed entries

### Broken Arrow

- **Type:** City
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-06-15, City Council enactment with emergency clause
- **Normalized date:** `2026-06-15` (exact)
- **Duration:** Until the earlier of December 31, 2026, or adoption of permanent regulations, with a possible extension totaling no more than six additional months
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ok-broken-arrow-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance No. 3929 (City of Broken Arrow), pausing new rezonings, special/conditional use permits, site plans, building permits, certificates of occupancy, and other approvals for data center uses; exempts vested projects, accessory uses, and facilities of 5 MW or less
- **What prompted it:** Development of permanent data center regulations
- **Affected projects:** —
- **Detailed status:** Prior review reported the moratorium active as of 2026-09-23. An October 20, 2026 city staff agenda describes its term as through December 31, 2026, or until permanent regulations are adopted; the item requested no action and does not establish later disposition. City Manager Michael Spurgeon gave a public update at the Aug. 18, 2026 City Council meeting confirming the moratorium 'will remain in effect until at least Dec. 31, 2026' and announcing a new Data Center Study Committee (led by Deputy City Attorney James Walters) to draft the eventual ordinance. As of late August 2026, no data center proposal was imminent (an earlier 51-acre site's letter of intent expired unrenewed), and Spurgeon said he may seek Council approval to extend the moratorium another six months, but no extension had been adopted as of 2026-09-23.
- **Outcome:** —

### Choctaw

- **Type:** City
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-07-21, Choctaw City Council, 6-1 vote (Councilman Cody Brewer dissenting on principle, not disagreement); accompanying emergency clause passed 6-1 (Councilman Brent Pendergraft dissenting)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-07-21` (exact)
- **Duration:** 12 months from the July 21, 2026 adoption date
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ok-choctaw-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Choctaw City Council ordinance/resolution (specific instrument number not located in captured coverage), imposing a 12-month moratorium on accepting data center applications within city limits, adopted with an accompanying emergency clause making it effective immediately
- **What prompted it:** Preemptive pause; no data center had submitted plans to build in Choctaw at adoption. Council discussed drafting an outright ban on data centers but opted for a one-year pause to evaluate possible further restrictions instead.
- **Affected projects:** None; no data centers had submitted plans to build in Choctaw as of adoption.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. 12-month moratorium adopted July 21, 2026, running through approximately July 21, 2027, while the city studies future data-center regulation; no developer had submitted plans in Choctaw at adoption or as of this pass.
- **Outcome:** Choctaw City Council approved a 12-month moratorium on data centers within city limits after discussing, and rejecting in favor of the pause, a proposed outright ban.

### Edmond

- **Type:** City
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-06-08 (Municode index identifies adoption of Ordinance 4091). Earlier review reported a unanimous vote and immediate effect; the signed final text and vote have not been independently verified.

- **Duration:** Runs through 2026-12-31; staff to report back to council at the 2, 3, and 5-month marks.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ok-edmond-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Municode index identifies Ordinance No. 4091 as adopted June 8, 2026, with a title declaring a moratorium until December 31, 2026 on applications for rezoning and building permits for data centers. An unsigned, unnumbered June 8 agenda draft defines covered data centers as AI-computing facilities contracting for 75 MW or more per facility or in aggregate behind a single point of interconnection; the signed final text and vote have not been independently verified. Earlier review reported a 5-0 vote and an emergency clause.
- **What prompted it:** No pending data center proposal in the city at time of adoption; preemptive pause to allow study of water, electricity, and infrastructure impacts and to draft permanent zoning rules.
- **Affected projects:** None pending at time of adoption.
- **Detailed status:** Prior review reported the moratorium active as of 2026-09-23 and found no amendment, extension, or repeal through that date. The ordinance index states a moratorium until December 31, 2026. A June 8 agenda draft provides for an earlier end on the effective date of duly adopted data-center regulations; the signed final text and subsequent city action have not been independently verified.
- **Outcome:** The ordinance index identifies adoption of a moratorium through December 31, 2026. Earlier review reported unanimous adoption and immediate effect; the signed final text, vote and subsequent city action have not been independently verified.

### Oklahoma City

- **Type:** City
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-04-21
- **Normalized date:** `2026-04-21` (exact)
- **Duration:** Until 2026-12-31, or earlier if data center zoning amendments are adopted
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ok-oklahoma-city-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance No. 28,071 (City of Oklahoma City), introduced, read, and passed with emergency on 2026-04-21 (Council Agenda Item XI.U), signed by the Mayor the same day; exempts pending rezoning applications PUD-2105 and PUD-2124. Amended 2026-05-19 by a 7-2 Council vote (per a City Manager memo amending Ordinance No. 28,071, adding a Section 7 definition limiting the moratorium to data centers with net-new electrical loads greater than 75 MW and a further exemption for the proposed project at 7725 N. Reno Ave. conditioned on potable-water use being limited to domestic/irrigation/fire-protection purposes); the specific ordinance number assigned to the May 19, 2026 amendment itself was not located.
- **What prompted it:** First large data center rezoning requests; no specific zoning use unit or regulations for data centers; concerns about water, electricity, noise, infrastructure, and other public impacts
- **Affected projects:** New applications for rezoning requests and permits, including building permits, for data center construction, expansion, or use; two pending rezoning requests are exempted
- **Detailed status:** Active, as amended, as of 2026-09-23; runs through Dec. 31, 2026 or the effective date of new data-center zoning-code amendments, whichever is earlier (Ordinance No. 28,071, Section 4). The May 19, 2026 amendment (7-2 vote) limited the moratorium to data centers with net-new electrical loads over 75 MW and added exemptions for the Expand Energy campus facility (serving Cerebras AI) and a facility at 7725 N. Reno Ave. No comprehensive data-center zoning use-unit had been adopted as of 2026-09-23 in any source reviewed in this pass, so the moratorium (as amended) remains in force; no further amendment or repeal was found.
- **Outcome:** City is using the pause to evaluate impacts and draft zoning code amendments for data centers

### Seminole Nation of Oklahoma

- **Type:** Tribal
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-03-07
- **Normalized date:** `2026-03-07` (exact)
- **Duration:** Indefinite by design, not merely undisclosed. Per KGOU reporting (June 25, 2026), the resolution's author, Rev. Chebon Kernell, originally drafted a ban on data-center discussions/inquiries/development, but 'that proposal turned into an indefinite moratorium at the suggestion of another council member.' The resolution's own phrase 'the moratorium period' (as quoted by Native News Online) therefore refers to an open-ended condition rather than a fixed numeric term that simply has not been published. The full resolution text remains unposted on sno-nsn.gov.
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ok-seminole-nation-of-oklahoma-2026`
- **Legal basis:** General Council of the Seminole Nation of Oklahoma, Tribal Resolution TR 2026-38, 'A Verbal Resolution... Implementing a Moratorium on the Advancement of Generative Artificial Intelligence Technology and Hyperscale Data Center Development within the Jurisdiction of the Seminole Nation of Oklahoma,' passed and approved at Mekusukey Mission on March 7, 2026 by a vote of 24 Yes, 0 No, 0 Abstaining (quorum of 15 present).
- **What prompted it:** Startup approach seeking an NDA and letter of intent to develop a data center on Seminole lands; environmental, water, sovereignty, and community-health concerns
- **Affected projects:** Any inquiries, discussions, or developments concerning data centers of any size within the Seminole Nation during the moratorium period
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. TR 2026-38 bars 'any inquiries, discussions, and/or developments concerning any entity seeking to develop a data center of any size within the Seminole Nation... during the moratorium period,' with no stated end date (open-ended by design, per KGOU/KOSU reporting on the resolution's drafting history). Multiple independent sources through Aug. 20, 2026 (KOSU, Turtle Talk blog, Current Tribal Law) continue to describe the moratorium as in force, with no rescission, amendment, or replacement framework identified as of 2026-09-23. No Tribal Council minutes confirming continued force were located on the Seminole Nation's own website in this pass either.
- **Outcome:** Moratorium adopted before project approval; permanent replacement framework not identified

### Shawnee

- **Type:** City
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** 2026-08-17 (Monday), Shawnee City Commission, unanimous 7-0 vote; resolution sponsored by Commissioner Chris Odneal
- **Normalized date:** `2026-08-17` (exact)
- **Duration:** From adoption through December 31, 2027
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Moratorium ID:** `ok-shawnee-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Shawnee City Commission resolution (specific resolution/instrument number not located in captured coverage), sponsored by Commissioner Chris Odneal, freezing new data center applications through Dec. 31, 2027
- **What prompted it:** Preemptive pause to allow city staff to study how large-scale data centers might strain local power and water systems, and to update city regulations, before accepting new proposals; city staff had initially estimated a 90-day study period would suffice, but Commissioners opted for a longer runway through the end of 2027. Discussions ahead of the vote also touched on land-use questions involving the Citizen Potawatomi Nation, whose tribal headquarters are in Shawnee.
- **Affected projects:** None named; no current applications were pending at adoption. Applies only to new applications going forward, not to any existing operating or under-construction projects.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23. Moratorium adopted Aug. 17, 2026 on a unanimous 7-0 vote, effective immediately, freezing new data-center applications through Dec. 31, 2027; does not affect any data center projects already operating or under construction in Shawnee. Staff committed to reporting findings within 90 days of adoption.
- **Outcome:** Shawnee City Commission adopted a moratorium freezing new data center applications through the end of 2027, directing staff to study power and water impacts and update city regulations before the pause lifts.

A redlined draft of the ordinance (marked 'JCB 3/25/26') shows the bill's caption and Section 4 term were amended from a flat '365-DAY' moratorium to a fixed expiration of 'December 31, 2026, or on the effective date of an ordinance amending data center regulations..., whichever is earlier'; the amendment also renumbered sections to add a Section 4 '60-DAY REPORTS' requirement for the Planning Office. This resolves the tension between the city's caption text and Tulsa Flyer's '9 months' reporting: the final adopted term is the Dec. 31, 2026 calendar date, not a literal 365-day count from adoption.

These are proposed regulations, not adopted amendments. The earlier redlined ordinance attachment provides an earlier-ending condition on qualifying regulations but has blank execution fields. Final executed instrument, operative conditions and later action through November 5 remain unresolved. ### HB 2992 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `ok-hb-2992-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Brad Boles; Sen. Grant Green; bipartisan coauthors; R / bipartisan
- **Recorded status:** Approved by the Governor on 2026-05-11. Enrolled section 8 states an effective date of July 1, 2026; section 9 declares an emergency and states effect upon passage and approval. An August 6 House report describes the act as effective July 1. The legal operation of these provisions and later amendments have not been independently resolved.
- **Provisions:** Data Center Customer Ratepayer Protection Act of 2026 requires separate utility tariffs and terms and cost-causation protections for qualifying new data centers, cryptocurrency mining and AI facilities contracting to add at least 75 MW after July 1, 2026. Qualifying land purchases outside municipalities or industrial development parks require notice within 60 days to the Corporation Commission, county commissioners and abutting owners, with penalties for noncompliance. A conference report was adopted before the bill was enrolled and approved.

### SB 259 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `ok-sb-259-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Sen. Brent Howard; House work by Rep. Carl Newton and Rep. Nick Archer; R
- **Recorded status:** Enacted; approved by Governor on 2026-05-20
- **Provisions:** Groundwater metering/permitting bill (originally introduced 2025-02-03, carried into the 2026 session of the same 60th Legislature), amended by committee substitute in both chambers to classify groundwater cooling at a data processing facility or data center through open-air evaporative cooling or other cooling that consumes groundwater through evaporation or discharge without recirculation as waste; permits require demonstration of closed-loop, dielectric immersion, or comparably low-consumptive technology that substantially recirculates groundwater and minimizes consumption. Passed Senate 36-11 (2026-03-25), passed House as amended 88-1 (2026-05-06), House amendments adopted by Senate 38-10 (2026-05-14), sent to Governor same day, approved 2026-05-20.
- **Mechanism / scope:** permitting_restriction; statewide
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2026-11-01
